# Snowflake SQL API¶

The Snowflake SQL API is a REST API that you can use to access and update data in a Snowflake database. You can use this API to develop custom applications and integrations that:

- Perform queries
- Manage your deployment (e.g. provision users and roles, create tables, etc.)

The Snowflake SQL API provides operations that you can use to:

- Submit SQL statements for execution.
- Check the status of the execution of a statement.
- Cancel the execution of a statement.

You can use this API to execute [standard queries](https://docs.snowflake.com/sql-reference/constructs) and most [DDL](https://docs.snowflake.com/sql-reference/sql-ddl-summary) and [DML](https://docs.snowflake.com/sql-reference/sql-dml) statements. See [Limitations of the SQL API](https://docs.snowflake.com/developer-guide/sql-api/intro#label-sql-api-limitations) for the types of statements that are not supported.

- **[Introduction to the SQL API](https://docs.snowflake.com/developer-guide/sql-api/intro)** Get an overview of the API.
- **[About the SQL API endpoints](https://docs.snowflake.com/developer-guide/sql-api/about-endpoints)** Learn about the endpoints that make up the API.
- **[Authenticating to the server](https://docs.snowflake.com/developer-guide/sql-api/authenticating)** Use OAuth or Key Pair to authenticate with the Snowflake server.
- **[Submitting a request to execute SQL statements](https://docs.snowflake.com/developer-guide/sql-api/submitting-requests)** Set up and submit requests using an API endpoint.
- **[Handling responses](https://docs.snowflake.com/developer-guide/sql-api/handling-responses)** Check request status and get results and other data after a request.
- **[Submitting multiple SQL statements in a single request](https://docs.snowflake.com/developer-guide/sql-api/submitting-multiple-statements)** Send multiple SQL statements in a single API request.
- **[Creating and calling stored procedures](https://docs.snowflake.com/developer-guide/sql-api/using-stored-procedures)** Create a stored procedure by specifying it in the body of a request.
- **[Using explicit transactions](https://docs.snowflake.com/developer-guide/sql-api/using-transactions)** Execute SQL in a transaction by specifying the start, end, and statements in the transaction.
- **[Getting details about an error](https://docs.snowflake.com/developer-guide/sql-api/handling-errors)** Retrieve error information.
- **[Canceling the execution of a SQL statement](https://docs.snowflake.com/developer-guide/sql-api/cancelling-requests)** Cancel SQL statement execution.
- **[Snowflake SQL API reference](https://docs.snowflake.com/developer-guide/sql-api/reference)** Read details about the operations, objects, HTTP headers, and response codes for this API.
